Technical Specs: Mailer Boxes
An overview of the standard customizations available for corrugated mailer boxes.
Corrugation
- E-fute
- Most common choice. Flute thickness of 1.2–2mm.
- B-flute
- Best for large boxes and heavy items. Flute thickness of 2.5–3mm.
Materials
Designs are printed on these base materials which is then glued to the corrugated board. All materials contain at least 50% post-consumer content (recycled materials).
- White
- Clay Coated News Back (CCNB) paper. Ideal for vibrant, full-color printing.
- Brown Kraft
- Unbleached brown paper. Best suited for simple black or white designs.
Color systems
- CMYK
- Cost-effective, standard full-color printing system.
- Pantone
- Premium color system used for exact brand color matching.
Coating
- Varnish
- An eco-friendly, water-based protective layer.
- Lamination
- A plastic layer that protects against scuffs, cracks, and tears.
Finishes
- Matte
- Smooth, non-reflective, softer look.
- Glossy
- High-shine reflective finish.
- Satin
- Semi-shiny blend between matte and glossy.
- Soft touch
- Premium matte look with a velvet-like texture.
Add-ons
Enhance your packaging designs with specialized printing treatments and accents.
- Foil stamping
- Metallic or colored foil layer applied with heat for a reflective shine.
- Spot UV
- Glossy coating applied to specific areas for high-contrast texture.
What is the minimum order quantity for custom mailer boxes?
The minimum order quantity for custom mailer boxes is 100 units. This MOQ applies to each unique box variation, meaning any change in size, material, or printed artwork counts as a separate production run of 100 boxes.
Where is your packaging produced?
We manufacture all of our packaging through a vetted network of trusted production partners in China, and ship everything directly from the factory to your doorstep.
What are your lead times?
Our standard production lead times typically take 12-16 days, though larger bulk orders can take 3-4 weeks depending on the overall volume and complexity of your packaging. Total delivery timelines will vary based on the shipping method you select.
How long does shipping take?
Shipping times depend entirely on the transport method you choose for your packaging. Air freight generally takes 1-3 weeks, while ocean freight ranges from 4-8 weeks. If you are on a tight deadline, you can split your shipment to send an initial batch via air and the remainder by sea.
Can PackMojo handle bulk production and recurring monthly shipments for eCommerce?
Yes, PackMojo supports growing eCommerce brands shipping hundreds of monthly orders through bulk production runs, volume-based pricing tiers, split shipments, and dedicated account support. You can set up split shipments to multiple locations, access dedicated support, and request custom volume pricing directly through our platform starting at just 100 units.
Can I purchase a sample before placing an order?
Absolutely. We offer several different sample types depending on what you need to test. Whether you just want to verify the physical size and fit of your packaging or need to check final colors and printed artwork, we've got you covered. You can explore all of our sample options here.
